title: KV sparse-index + compact-occupancy-bitmap: proposal and heuristics
body:
Summary:
This note proposes a complementary KV cache architecture centered on a sparse-chunk index and a compact-occupancy bitmap (COB) to reduce fragmentation, simplify compaction, and make eviction size-aware. The design targets workloads with heterogeneous KV entry sizes (small chat-token entries to multi-kB embeddings), high concurrency, and NUMA-separated GPU host memory pools.

Goals:
- Reduce long-tail memory fragmentation without heavy stop-the-world compaction.
- Support efficient size-aware eviction and fast prefix/KV cache lookups.
- Make compaction incremental, locality-friendly, and observable.
- Interoperate with existing continuous-batching and KV-cache APIs with minimal client changes.

Background / Motivation:
Our current slab and slabless proposals address many cases but struggle when workloads mix very different KV sizes and when allocations/evictions create many small free holes. Heavy-handed compaction introduces latency spikes; purely opportunistic reuse leaves memory unusable. The sparse-index + COB approach aims to create a compacted high-level view of occupancy while keeping per-chunk operations lightweight.

High-level idea:
- Physical memory is divided into fixed-size chunks (e.g., 64KB by default, param by profile). Each chunk holds many KV entries and has a small header in a chunk metadata array.
- A sparse-chunk index maps ModelShardID / RequestID / KV-key -> (chunk_id, slot_metadata). The index is optimized for lookups and eviction marking, not for storing raw payloads.
- A compact-occupancy bitmap (COB) is maintained per-NUMA arena and summarizes chunk-level free vs occupied granularity plus a tight packing score used for compaction heuristics. COB is a contiguous bitmap (1 bit per chunk primary occupancy + 3–5 bits of packed score per chunk).
- Compaction proceeds at chunk granularity: a micro-coalescer relocates live entries from low-packing-score chunks into higher packing-score targets when thresholds are crossed. Relocation operates in small epochs and uses copy-on-write fast lanes to avoid blocking reads.

Key data structures (concise):
- chunk_table[]: array of chunk headers (chunk_id => base_addr, numa_affinity, packed_score, generation, lock_state).
- COB (CompactOccupancyBitmap): linear buffer of words; each chunk has: occupied_bit, packed_score_nibble (0-15), eviction_hint_bit. The COB is cheap to scan with popcount and vector ops.
- sparse_index: sharded hash map (per-NUMA / per-core) mapping KV digest -> compact pointer (chunk_id + offset + small tag). The pointer is 64-bit to stay compact.
- relocation_log: lightweight ring of pending relocations for background workers; contains source_chunk, dest_chunk, bytes_moved, epoch_id.

Allocation and freelist strategy:
- Allocation prefers chunks with packing_score >= target and free space; fast-path uses per-core freelists of chunk slots to reduce contention.
- We maintain two freelist types per arena: fast_buckets for small allocs (<512B) and sparse_chunks for larger ones. This hybrid keeps small allocations cheap while still allowing packing.
- When a free request cannot be satisfied in-core, allocator scans COB words for chunks with free space. Scans use a best-effort vectorized search (scan few words, give up and fallback to global allocator).

Eviction policy (size-aware MRU-LRU hybrid):
- Each KV entry has a compact recency tag embedded in the sparse_index (8-bit epoch counter) and a size class.
- Evictor works at chunk granularity for low overhead: when we need capacity, we pick candidate chunks by (low packed_score, low recent_access_sum, high stale_ratio). Within a chunk we evict entire small entries first and mark large entries for relocation if they are frequently accessed.
- To support low tail latency, eviction runs asynchronously with a fast synchronous fallback that can instantly free whole chunks (evict-all) when under extreme pressure.

Compaction / fragmentation mitigation:
- Packing score: computed as occupancy_ratio * weighted_size_utilization - fragmentation_penalty. Weighted_size_utilization biases moving many small entries together into a target chunk to reduce small holes.
- Micro-coalescer: background workers pick low-score chunks and attempt to move live entries into target chunks with enough slack. Moves are atomic at KV granularity using relocation epochs.
- Relocation epoch model: new readers/writers see a tag; a brief copy-on-write window ensures an in-flight lookup either reads old location or new one. Metadata updates are CAS on sparse_index pointer. Epochs are short (tunable ms range).
- Incremental compaction: limit bytes moved per worker per second to avoid noisy neighbors. Use backoff if eviction/compaction reduces throughput on the serving path.

NUMA and placement considerations:
- COB is per-NUMA arena to limit cross-node scans. chunk_table has numa_affinity field and relocation prefers same-NUMA targets when possible.
- For bursts that cross NUMA boundaries, we permit cross-NUMA allocation but mark chunk affinity to allow later consolidation during lower load.

Concurrency model and safety:
- Sparse_index is sharded by high bits of key digest; each shard has its own lock/lock-free CAS path for updates. Lookups are read-mostly and use relaxed memory ordering.
- Chunk header updates (packed_score, free_space) are updated with atomic ops; the COB words are updated with atomic fetch-or/fetch-and operations to support lockless scans.
- Relocation uses fine-grained per-entry locks (or CAS on pointer) + a short-lived destination reservation to avoid double-copy races.

Observability / metrics (first-class):
- chunk_count, free_chunks, avg_packing_score, packing_score_histogram, bytes_moved/sec, relocation_ops/sec, compaction_backoff_seconds, fragmentation_ratio (free_holes_bytes / total_bytes).
- Per-model & per-shard breakdowns: eviction_rate_by_model, average_entry_size_by_model, hot_chunk_percent_by_model.
- Tracing: a relocation trace with pre/post mapping and time spent, emitted to Console for rollouts and SLO debugging.

Tradeoffs and rationale:
- Chunk granularity simplifies compaction and reduces metadata overhead vs fully variable-size compaction. 64KB chosen as a sweet spot for many embedding + kv-size mixes, but tunable per workload.
- COB allows fast vector scans and cheap heuristics; it is an approximation (packing_score is coarse) but sufficient to prioritize compaction work without scanning payloads.
- Relocation epochs and copy-on-write add small latency to writes while preventing stop-the-world moves. This favors predictable tail latency over maximal compaction efficiency.

Migration plan (incremental rollout):
1) Implement COB + chunk_table read-only view in parallel with existing slab allocator; collect metrics for packing_score distribution on real workloads.
2) Add allocator fast-path that prefers high-score chunks; run in conservative mode (no relocation) to validate allocation behavior.
3) Introduce micro-coalescer as an opt-in background worker with low default throughput cap.
4) Gradually enable size-aware eviction and synchronous fallback on canary hosts, monitor Console metrics and tracing.
5) If stable, flip default on for dedicated pools and expose chunk_size tuning in Dedicated/Private configs.

Open questions / future work:
- Should packing_score weighting be model-aware? (e.g., embeddings vs chat token key distributions) Likely yes; we can attach model metadata to chunks for better heuristics.
- Explore hardware-accelerated bitmap scans (AVX/NEON) in native allocator hot path.
- Investigate combining fingerprinted small-entry packing (micro-slab inside chunk) to further reduce internal fragmentation for <64B items.

Action items (next 4 weeks):
- Prototype COB layout and a lightweight COB scanner (owner: David Kim, PR target: end of sprint).
- Add chunk_table and a chunk-scoring exporter to Console (owner: Aisha Patel).
- Create JIRA tickets for relocation epoch API and sparse_index pointer format (owner: Sofia Martinez).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally a hybrid design: not a slab-slayer or slab-only replacement. It is intended to sit alongside slab tactics and be used where mixed sizes + long-lived fragmentation dominate costs.
- Tradeoff tuning will be workload-dependent; expect per-customer defaults for Dedicated/Private deployments.

References / related work:
- prior internal notes on slabless pools and compact allocators (see linked PR and JIRA).
- academic: "Region-oriented heap compaction for concurrent systems" (background for relocation epoch pattern).

End.
